chunks: And as for what was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): regarding

the woman who says to her husband, 'My slave girl is for you,' he said, 'It is not permissible for him to have her private part (for sexual use) unless she sells it to him or gifts it to him.' This report is understood to mean that when she says to him, 'It is for you,' she means what is below the private part (i.e., for service), because it is known from the custom of women that they do not make their husbands permissible in sexual intercourse with their slave girls, and if the matter is thus, it is not permissible for him to have her private part in any case. As for the master (owner), it is not permissible for him to make his slave permissible in sexual intercourse with his slave girl except through a contract (of ownership/possession).
ai.seo_question: Does a wife giving her slave girl to her husband automatically grant him sexual rights over her?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of 'customary understanding' (al-'urf) to interpret the wife's declaration, distinguishing between granting service and granting sexual possession, a nuance critical in Shia jurisprudence regarding concubinage. The text further clarifies that while a master may grant his slave girl to another, the recipient must establish a valid contract to legitimize the sexual relationship, ensuring the transition from ownership to marital-like rights is legally sound.
